title: Windows Gets Open-Weight A.I. Like China's DeepSeek and Nvidia's Nemotron
key_facts: Microsoft declares Windows a platform for 'hybrid intelligence', with AI agents running on the PC or in the cloud, depending on the task.
Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), sandboxes that limit which files and networks an agent can reach, are generally available on Windows 11.
Open-weight models such as DeepSeek and Nvidia's Nemotron are being brought to the PC; GitHub's HydraFusion routes tasks to the right model, as an experimental preview later in October.
Copilot's new powers, such as organising files, come only to Copilot+ PCs and roll out over the coming months; Microsoft has not given dates per country.
Windows Search gets commands such as 'switch to dark mode', now rolling out to Windows Insiders in the experimental channel.
Speed claims for the Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia's RTX Spark chip come from tests commissioned or run by Microsoft and Nvidia.
quote_evidence: The figures, however, come from tests commissioned or run by Microsoft and Nvidia themselves, using preproduction devices.
The limits: The features are coming only to Copilot+ PCs and are set to roll out over the coming months.
Microsoft has not said when which feature will arrive on which device in which country.
why_it_matters_hint: PC users and businesses get more control over AI agents, but the features arrive slowly and unevenly.
